original_question: Determine whether particle trajectories of Euler flows are analytic in time in arbitrary dimension, and how that analyticity depends on the presence and analyticity of boundaries. This includes clarifying the status of Yudovich-class trajectories, which are known to be Gevrey regular but not known to be analytic.
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Problem 12 on time-analyticity of Euler particle trajectories in any dimension and its dependence on boundary analyticity, together with the immediately related Yudovich-trajectory question in Remark 6.2. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the two main components actually singled out by the paper: the open problem of whether Euler particle trajectories are analytic in time in arbitrary dimension, and the dependence of that statement on analyticity of the boundary; it also correctly brings in the separate but adjacent Yudovich question, for which the paper says Gevrey regularity is known while analyticity remains open. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
missing_details: The exact official target is Problem 12 in Section 6.1; the Yudovich issue is not part of the formal statement of Problem 12, but is posed immediately afterward as a related problem in Remark 6.2. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: incompressible Euler flow on a manifold or domain M, rather than just 'Euler flows' abstractly. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The paper's notion of particle trajectory is explicit and should be included: a curve x(t) satisfying dx/dt = u(t, x(t)). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The nearby known theorem being extended is 2-dimensional: M is a compact real-analytic 2-manifold or a bounded domain with analytic boundary, u is of Sobolev class H^s with s > 2, and when boundary is present the slip/tangency condition is imposed. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

Problem 12 itself does not specify a general-dimensional Sobolev threshold; it relies on the surrounding Theorem 6.1 setup for the precise regularity assumptions in the established 2D case. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

A fully faithful stand-alone version should note the partial positive results recorded in Remark 6.2: for boundaryless R^d, analyticity is already proved for d = 2 and 3, and the authors comment that higher dimensions without boundary do not appear fundamentally harder. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

For the boundary aspect, the immediate context also notes Nadirashvili's local stationary 2D result, which is independent of whether the boundary is analytic; that nuance explains why boundary analyticity is isolated as an issue. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

For the Yudovich clause, the paper defines the class by divergence-free u with ||curl u||_{L^∞} < ∞, notes uniqueness of trajectories via the Osgood property, and says only Gevrey time-regularity is known, with sharpness unknown. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
No algebraic data such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency are relevant here; the missing implicit data are geometric and PDE hypotheses instead.
refined_question: Extend the analyticity result of Theorem 6.1 to higher-dimensional incompressible Euler flows: if u(t, x) is a sufficiently regular/classical Euler solution on an n-dimensional manifold or domain M, with slip boundary condition when ∂M is nonempty, and x(t) is a particle trajectory solving dx/dt = u(t, x(t)), must x(t) be real-analytic in time for every n? If M has boundary, does the answer depend on whether ∂M is real-analytic? Relatedly, in the Yudovich class (divergence-free u with ||curl u||_{L^∞} < ∞, so trajectories are unique), can the currently known Gevrey time-regularity of trajectories be upgraded to real analyticity?
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful refinement because the exact official open problem matching your draft is Problem 12 in Section 6.1, and its wording is precisely about analyticity in time of particle trajectories in any dimension and the role of boundary analyticity. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf)) The surrounding context that makes the problem stand-alone is Theorem 6.1, where the already proved case is a 2D compact real-analytic manifold or bounded domain with analytic boundary, for Euler solutions u in H^s with s > 2, with particle trajectories defined by dx/dt = u(t, x(t)). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf)) Your draft's final sentence also belongs in scope, but only as an adjacent add-on: Remark 6.2 explicitly raises the separate related question of analyticity for Yudovich trajectories and states that only Gevrey regularity is known, with unknown sharpness. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf)) The same remark records that analyticity without boundary is already known in R^d for d = 2 and 3, so the refined version should not imply that the entire boundaryless arbitrary-dimensional problem is untouched. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
